body: We could fix this by lazily initializing `rAF` polyfill, but now that I think of it, it seems unfortunate that merely importing `findDOMNode` (which is likely what components do) runs the whole client reconciler init code.

@gaearon Shouldn't it have been caught in the [unit test](https://github.com/facebook/react/blob/master/src/renderers/dom/shared/__tests__/findDOMNode-test.js)

Also, more importantly, isn't requiring `react-dom` and running `findDOMNode` on server an anti-pattern, and that components must avoid them in hooks that run on the server?

>Also, more importantly, isn't requiring react-dom and running findDOMNode on server an anti-pattern, and that components must avoid them in hooks that run on the server?

You shouldn't run it on the server, but importing it is fine. Otherwise how would you write a component that uses `findDOMNode` on the client but still works on the server?

>Shouldn't it have been caught in the unit test

No, the test doesn’t catch this because we set up a global rAF polyfill as part of our testing environment.

issue.title: React fiber support

repository.name: storybook
repository.description: Storybook is the industry standard workshop for building, documenting, and testing UI components in isolation

issue.body:
> Issue #724

😮 Problem
===

Let's assume you use `react@16.x.y(-alpha-z)` and you write a story as similar as this one:

```js
storiesOf('Fiber rendering', module)
  .add('with array', () => 
    ['Hello Button', '😀 😎 👍 💯'].map(label => 
      <Button onClick={action(`clicked(${label})`)} key={label}>{label}</Button>
    )
  )
  .add('with string', () => 'Yay!')
  .add('with number', () => 1337)
  .add('with invalid render (object)', () => ({ invalid: true }));
```

In the React preview
---

There is a specific check on the `element` to render in the preview which prevents using the new "rendering features" of React Fiber:  array, string, number.

If you write a story as similar as the one shown above, the UI will throw errors as seen [in this screencast](https://cl.ly/011L1S3c2V35).

In Storyshots (-> Jest -> Node)
---

`requestAnimationFrame` is used in React Fiber, and doesn't exist in Node env, and so Jest (`storyshots`). It appears that it's something that needs to be fixed at the whole app level, it's not only a Storyshots issue. [See screenshot](https://cl.ly/0S3T0r1C0D09).

✍️ What I did
===

on the UI
--- 

Simply remove the check, and let `ReactDOM` throws an error if the element is invalid.

Here is a screencast of what's happening without this check:

**Without the `element.type === undefined` check:**

![screencast](https://d3vv6lp55qjaqc.cloudfront.net/items/2Q0d3l1y061c3Y1o160R/Screen%20Recording%202017-07-10%20at%2007.17%20AM.gif?X-CloudApp-Visitor-Id=2680119&v=24fe45ff)

for Storyshots (/ Jest)
---

If somebody decides to use React Fiber and Jest, they needs to manually mock `requestAnimationFrame` (at the moment! 🤙).

We can do like explained in this comment: https://github.com/facebook/react/issues/9102#issuecomment-283873039.

```js
// __mocks__/react.js
global.window = global;
window.addEventListener = () => {};
window.requestAnimationFrame = () => {
  throw new Error('requestAnimationFrame is not supported in Node');
};
```

📟 How to test
===

Setup using the `examples/test-cra` app
---

```sh
git clone https://github.com/storybooks/storybook
cd storybook
git checkout 724-react-fiber-support
cd examples/test-cra
yarn add react@alpha react-dom@alpha
yarn add --dev react-test-renderer@alpha
```

Add the following story to `stories/index.js`:
```js
storiesOf('Fiber rendering', module)
  .add('with array', () => 
    ['Hello Button', '😀 😎 👍 💯'].map(label => 
      <Button onClick={action(`clicked(${label})`)} key={label}>{label}</Button>
    )
  )
  .add('with string', () => 'Yay!')
  .add('with number', () => 1337)
  .add('with invalid render (object)', () => ({ invalid: true }));
```

Preview test
---

```sh
yarn storybook
```

Then, go to http://localhost:9009.


Storyshots test
---

Create a `__mocks_` folder in the root folder and add a `react.js` file in it:

```sh
mkdir __mocks__
touch react.js
```

Add the following in `react.js`:
```js
global.window = global;
window.addEventListener = () => {};
window.requestAnimationFrame = () => {
  throw new Error('requestAnimationFrame is not supported in Node');
};
```

```sh
yarn test
```

❓ Questions
===

Should we keep the preview check and replace it by a function like `isValidElement` checking whether it's an element, a number, a string, or an array (and at elements inside it)?  

What do you think? 🤔
